title: Antimicrobial Peptides Produced by Selective Pressure Incorporation of Non-canonical Amino Acids
protocol: Clone the genes for nisin biosynthesis (nisABC) from L. lactis.
Transfer the cloned genes into T7-based plasmid expression vectors.
Place the gene for the precursor peptide (nisA) on a pET-3a vector conferring ampicillin resistance.
Mutate the codons of the last four amino acids (ASPR) in nisA to encode VSLR to ensure proper prepeptide processing by NisP.
Add a hexa-histidine tag flanked by linker residues at the N-terminus for purification purposes.
Place genes for dehydratase (nisB) and cyclase (nisC) on vector pRSFDuet-1, which confers kanamycin resistance.
Use standard heat-shock protocol to transform the proline auxotrophic E. coli strain with the plasmids pET-3a nisA(VSLR) and pRSFDuet-1 nisBC.
Use electroporation to transform the proline auxotrophic E. coli strain with the plasmids pET-3a nisA(VSLR) and pRSFDuet-1 nisBC.
Pipette 25-100 µl of transformed cell suspension onto agar plates containing ampicillin, kanamycin and 1% (w/v) glucose.
Use a plate spreader or glass beads to spread the solution evenly on the plates.
Incubate plates overnight at 37 °C.
Inoculate single colony into 10 ml LB medium containing ampicillin, kanamycin and 1% (w/v) glucose in a 50 ml flask.
Shake culture overnight (12-16 h) at 37 °C and 200 rpm.
Mix 250 µl sterile 80% glycerol with 550 µl culture in a 2 ml tube.
Store the mixed solution as frozen cell stock at -80 °C.
Dissolve 0.5 g Phe, Trp and Tyr in 100 ml ddH2O with a few drops of concentrated HCl until dissolution.
Weigh out 0.5 g of each of the remaining 16 amino acids.
Mix the weighed amino acids with 22 ml of 1 M KH2PO4 and 48 ml of 1 M K2HPO4.
Add ddH2O to ~800 ml.
Stir until the solution becomes clear.
Mix the dissolved Phe, Trp, and Tyr.
Adjust the volume of the solution to 1 L with ddH2O.
Sterilize the amino acid mixture by vacuum filtration with a bottle top filter unit.
Prepare 1 M stock solutions of (NH4)2SO4, KH2PO4, K2HPO4, MgSO4.
Prepare a 5 M stock solution of NaCl.
Autoclave all prepared stock solutions to sterilize.
Prepare 50 mL stocks of D-glucose at 1 M concentration.
Dissolve CaCl2 at a concentration of 1 g/L in 50 mL and filter sterilize.
Dissolve FeCl2 at a concentration of 1 g/L in 50 mL and filter sterilize.
Dissolve thiamine at a concentration of 10 g/L in 50 mL and filter sterilize.
Dissolve biotin at a concentration of 10 mg/L in 50 mL and filter sterilize.
Prepare trace elements (CuSO4, ZnCl2, MnCl2, (NH4)2MoO4) at 1 mg/L concentration and filter sterilize.
Mix all stock solutions to obtain a final concentration of 7.5 mM (NH4)2SO4.
Ensure the solution contains 1.7 mM NaCl, 22 mM KH2PO4, 50 mM K2HPO4, and 1 mM MgSO4.
Add 20 mM D-glucose to the solution.
Include 50 mg/L amino acid mix in the final mixture.
Add 1 µg/L CaCl2 to the stock solutions.
Add 1 µg/L FeCl2 to the stock solutions.
Include 10 µg/L thiamine in the final mixture.
Add 10 mg/L biotin to the solution.
Include trace elements at a concentration of 0.01 µg/mL.
Grow cells in LB complex medium containing all cAAs, ampicillin, kanamycin, and 1% glucose.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C and 200 rpm.
Inoculate 1 L of sterile fresh medium with 10 mL overnight culture (1% v/v) and incubate at 37 °C and 200 rpm until OD600 = 0.5.
Centrifuge the culture at 4 °C for 15 min at 4,500 x g.
Pour off the supernatant and resuspend the pellet with 20 mL of NMM19 medium containing antibiotics and 1% glucose.
Centrifuge again at 4 °C for 10 min at 4,500 x g.
Resuspend cell pellet in 500 mL of the same medium and incubate at 30 °C and 200 rpm for 1 h.
Divide the culture into equal parts for each ncAA.
Induce each culture with 1 mM IPTG.
Supply 1 mM proline analogs to each induced culture (4S/R-fluoroproline, 4S/R-hydroxyproline or 4S/R-methanoproline).
Incubate overnight at 28 °C and 200 rpm.
Centrifuge the cell cultures in 50 mL tubes at 4 °C for 20 min at 5,000 x g.
Pour off the supernatant.
Store pellets at -80 °C until purification.
Prepare 250 mL of binding buffer (5 M GuHCl, 300 mM NaCl, 25 mM Tris, pH 7.4).
Prepare 250 mL of wash buffer (300 mM NaCl, 25 mM Tris, 25 mM imidazole, pH 7.4).
Prepare 250 mL of elution buffer (300 mM NaCl, 25 mM Tris, 250 mM imidazole, pH 7.4).
Add 12 mL binding buffer to each centrifuge tube and resuspend by vortexing.
Submerge the tip of the sonicator probe into the cell suspension.
Set sonicator at 40% amplitude with pulse of 1 s on / 5 s off for 15 min.
Clean the sonicator tip between samples with 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge the lysed cell suspension at 4 °C for 40 min at 15,000 x g to pellet cell debris.
Transfer the supernatants to a new reaction tube.
Wash the cartridge with 5 column volumes of ddH2O to remove storage buffer.
Equilibrate with 10 cv of binding buffer.
Process cell lysate using a syringe filter to remove particles.
Apply the filtered sample to the cartridge.
Wash with 15 cv of wash buffer to remove nonspecific and unbound material.
Elute with 10 cv of elution buffer, collecting 1 mL fractions in 1.5 mL tubes.
Store the collected fractions at 4 °C for short-term storage (up to 3 days) or at -20 °C for longer-term storage.
Wash the cartridge with 10 cv of ddH2O followed by 5 cv of 20% ethanol before storage.
Prepare a peptide solution in step 4.3 for LC-ESI-TOF Mass Spectrometric Analysis.
Perform HPLC separation on a C5 column using a mobile phase gradient from 5-80% B over 20 min, where water and acetonitrile are both supplemented with 0.1% formic acid.
Use appropriate software to deconvolute the measured mass spectra and calculate different peptide charge states.
Compare the observed peptide species mass to the calculated wild-type mass altered by cAA → ncAA substitution.
Take into account that the linear prepeptide is posttranslationally modified by eight dehydrations (-8 H2O) and five cyclizations.
Prepare an overnight culture of the indicator strain L. lactis NZ9000 carrying plasmid pNG nisPT44 in M17 broth with 1% glucose and 5 µg/mL chloramphenicol at 30 °C.
Measure OD600 of the bacterial culture.
Inoculate fresh medium to achieve an OD600 = 0.1 and incubate until OD600 = 0.4-0.6.
Place the flask on ice after reaching the desired OD600.
Weigh out 4.5 g agar in a glass media bottle and add 300 mL ddH2O, mix, and autoclave.
Prepare 2x M17 broth in 300 mL ddH2O and autoclave.
Mix 25 mL 2x M17 broth containing 10 µg/mL chloramphenicol and 2% glucose with 1 mL L. lactis preculture (4% v/v).
Add 25 mL molten 1.5% agar to the mixture, ensuring the agar is at approximately 50 °C.
Pour the mixture onto GM17-agar plates under sterile conditions.
Pour the solution into a large petri dish.
Dry plates for 10-15 min.
Sterilize the ends of a glass Pasteur pipette by flame.
Wait for it to cool down, then use the wide end to create holes in the solidified GM17-agar.
Take 1 mL of the E. coli expression cultures and centrifuge for 3 min at 7,000 x g.
Aspirate the remaining medium and resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL Na-P buffer.
Sonicate the samples on ice with a sonicator set at 30 % amplitude with pulse of 1 s on and 5 s off for 3 min.
Centrifuge the cell lysate for 10 min at 13,000 x g to pellet cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant to a new reaction tube on ice.
Dilute and normalize the cell extract supernatants to 1 mL OD600 = 0.6 with Na-P buffer.
Add 40 µL of each normalized sample into a hole of the indicator agar plate.
Use chloramphenicol at 400 µg/mL as antibacterial control compound.
Use elution buffer as a negative control.
Incubate the plate overnight at 30 °C.
Prepare 10 mM Nile red stock solution in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Grow L. lactis indicator strain to OD600 = 1.0.
Centrifuge 1 mL culture for 3 min at 4 °C and 5,000 x g.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Centrifuge again and resuspend once more in PBS.
Add 1 µL Nile red stock solution to the cells.
Mix gently with the Nile red solution.
Add 30 µL of the cell preparation onto a cover slide while exciting at 520 nm.
Set acquisition time to 0.2 s, kinetic series to 0.1 Hz, and series length to 200 images.
Add 0.3 - 1.5 µL of cell lysate or IMAC sample.
Monitor fluorescence emission at λ ≥ 560 nm.
Record the fluorescence emission data.
